Can Carrier ReuseIthaca, NY · Cornell Sustainability Consultants
Student-run reuse program · since August 2025

Drink. Return. Repeat.

Plastic can carriers can't be recycled in Ithaca, so most end up in the trash after one use. We collect them at drop-off boxes around town, sort them, and return them to local breweries to hold new cans.

What's a can carrier?

The plastic topper on a 4- or 6-pack

Can carriers are hard plastic toppers that snap onto beer and soda cans. They're durable enough to use many times, but Ithaca has no way to recycle them. Every carrier that goes back to a brewery is one they don't have to buy new, saving about $0.15 each.

See how the program works
Our work

From drop-off box to a new four-pack

We built the collection system from scratch in 2025–26: bins, signage, a pickup schedule with partners, and a way to track how full each bin gets.

Drop off

Shoppers leave used carriers in a box at GreenStar, Personal Best, Ithaca Bakery or Lev Kitchen.

Collect & sort

Our team picks them up and sorts by color, since some breweries only reuse certain colors.

Return

Clean carriers go back to Personal Best and other local breweries.

Reuse & measure

Breweries put them on new cans. Partners send a bin photo every two weeks so we can track volume.

Partners & collection sites

Businesses that keep carriers in circulation

Collection partners host our drop-off boxes. Reuse partners put the carriers back on cans. We're always looking for more of both.

Collection partner · 3 stores

GreenStar Food Co+op

Ithaca's community grocery co-op hosts drop-off boxes at all three of its stores. Carriers are gathered at one primary store for pickup.

greenstar.coop ↗Store hours and locations
Collection + reuse partner

Personal Best Brewing

Hosts a collection box in its taproom and reuses the carriers we return on its own cans. Our pilot ran collection, pickup and reuse end to end here.

How we measure

The visual fill method

  • Each three-tier bin holds about 200 carriers; every tier is roughly 33%.
  • Partners send a bin photo every two weeks through a Google Form.
  • We count carriers from the photo and log the fill percentage.
  • Savings estimates follow the Vermont Can Carrier Reuse Program model.
  • Coming soon: we're switching to AI-powered photo reading, which counts carriers from each bin photo automatically for more accurate data.
